title: Describe the tipper assignment and entrance-queue flow for a full tote (round-robin to enabled tippers)
summary: When a full tote on an AGV reaches the sorter, Execute assigns a specific tipper using round-robin among available enabled tippers serviced by the relevant queue. The AGV is then routed to the tipper entrance queue; when the AGV reaches the front of that entrance queue and the tipper becomes available, the AGV is sent to the tipper for the tip/clamp cycle.
when_to_use: Use this procedure to explain (and communicate) the tote-to-tipper assignment and entrance-queue gating behavior for a full tote on an AGV: round-robin selection among available enabled tippers serviced by the queue, followed by entrance-queue waiting until the tipper is available.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Use this flow description to communicate how Execute selects a tipper and how the AGV is gated by the tipper entrance queue until the tipper becomes available.
access_or_tools_needed: Training video segment transcript (00:28:37.000 to 00:32:10.000) for tipper assignment and queueing rules

steps.title: Use the full-tote-to-sorter starting point
steps.purpose: Establish the correct starting condition for the flow (a full tote on an AGV reaching the sorter).
steps.instruction: Identify the scenario as: a full tote sits in the aisle on an AGV and reaches the sorter.
steps.expected_result: You can describe the flow starting from the moment the full tote reaches the sorter (not from a later stage such as tipper completion).
steps.healthy_condition: The described starting point is explicitly the full tote on an AGV reaching the sorter.
steps.failure_condition: You describe the flow starting from a different point (e.g., after the tipper has already clamped/tipped, or from a charger/hospital state).

actions.label: State the starting condition
actions.exact_action: “A full tote now sits in the aisle on an AGV. When it reaches the sorter …”

steps.title: Identify the tipper assignment step (Execute assigns a specific tipper)
steps.purpose: Clarify which system component performs the tipper selection at the sorter.
steps.instruction: Explain that when the AGV reaches the sorter, Execute assigns a specific tipper.
steps.expected_result: Your explanation states that Execute assigns a specific tipper at the sorter arrival point.
steps.healthy_condition: The assignment is attributed to Execute (not to the operator or to the tipper controller).
steps.failure_condition: You attribute tipper assignment to the wrong actor (e.g., operator decision) or omit the Execute assignment step.

actions.label: Name the assignment actor
actions.exact_action: “When the AGV reaches the sorter, execute is assigned a specific tipper.”

steps.title: Apply the selection rule (round-robin among available enabled tippers serviced by this queue)
steps.purpose: Provide the concrete selection logic used to choose which tipper Execute assigns.
steps.instruction: Explain that the tipper selection uses round-robin to available enabled tippers serviced by this queue.
steps.expected_result: You can state: round-robin selection among available enabled tippers serviced by the queue.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation includes both constraints: (1) available and (2) enabled, and ties them to the queue servicing set.
steps.failure_condition: You describe selection without the round-robin rule, or without the available/enabled constraints.

actions.label: State the round-robin rule
actions.exact_action: “We used round Robin to the available enabled tippers serviced by this queue.”

steps.title: Apply the queueing rule (send AGV to the tipper entrance queue)
steps.purpose: Explain how the AGV is routed after tipper assignment.
steps.instruction: Explain that after Execute assigns the tipper, the AGV is sent to the tipper entrance queue.
steps.expected_result: Your explanation states that the AGV is sent to the tipper entrance queue after tipper assignment.
steps.healthy_condition: The routing step is described as: assigned tipper -> sent to tipper entrance queue.
steps.failure_condition: You describe the AGV going directly to the tipper without entrance-queue gating.

actions.label: State the routing to entrance queue
actions.exact_action: “This AGV is then sent to the tipper entrance queue.”

steps.title: Apply entrance-queue gating (front of entrance queue + tipper availability -> send to tipper)
steps.purpose: Explain the condition that releases the AGV from the entrance queue to the tipper.
steps.instruction: Explain that when the AGV reaches the front of the tipper entrance queue and the tipper becomes available, the AGV is sent to the tipper.
steps.expected_result: You can state the gating condition: front-of-entrance-queue AND tipper availability triggers sending the AGV to the tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation includes both the queue position (front) and the availability condition (tipper becomes available).
steps.failure_condition: You describe gating based only on queue position or only on tipper availability.

actions.label: State the release condition
actions.exact_action: “When the AGV reaches the front of the tipper entrance queue and the tipper becomes available, the AGB is sent to the tipper.”

success_criteria: You can accurately explain the full-tote flow: Execute assigns a specific tipper using round-robin among available enabled tippers serviced by the queue, then routes the AGV to the tipper entrance queue.
You can accurately explain the entrance-queue release condition: when the AGV reaches the front of the tipper entrance queue and the tipper becomes available, the AGV is sent to the tipper.
healthy_conditions: Explanation includes: Execute assignment at sorter arrival, round-robin among available enabled tippers serviced by the queue, AGV sent to tipper entrance queue, and release at front-of-entrance-queue when tipper becomes available.
failure_conditions: Explanation contradicts the round-robin/availability mechanism (e.g., claims a fixed tipper or ignores enabled/available constraints).
Explanation omits the entrance-queue gating step or replaces it with a direct routing to the tipper.
escalation_guidance: If observed tipper assignment behavior contradicts the round-robin/availability explanation, escalate for deeper system evidence beyond this training segment.
